reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse any statement of a USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure (the paragraphs of the declarative section the USE heads) that stores into the storage of a control data item of any report: the item itself, a group containing it, a subordinate item, a REDEFINES/RENAMES or reference-modified view sharing a byte, or an implicit store (READ record area, POINTER/TALLYING/REMAINDER/VARYING operands), and must admit stores that touch no byte of one.

edition-consulted.switches: ctx.Edition.DialectLevel selects only the diagnostic's wording (must/shall) and the clause it cites (§1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR4 below 2002); the decision is edition-free

reader.edition-search: Read CheckControlDataStores, SameStorageLine, the StatementBinder.BindStatement call site and EnclosingContext.InBeforeReportingProcedure; grepped them for Edition/DialectLevel/CobolVersion: the only consults are the message text. CheckControlDataReferences (a separate 1985-only rule, XIII.3.20.3 SR5) is gated on DialectLevel < 2002 but is not this rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same 19 statements are refused at --std 85 and --std 2023 (COBOL2378), only the cited clause in the message differs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise MOVE CORRESPONDING/ADD/SUBTRACT CORR/INITIALIZE REPLACING (legal side), a READ into the record area and a RANDOM READ setting a RELATIVE KEY; not exercised by them: arithmetic GIVING/REMAINDER, STRING/UNSTRING/INSPECT/ACCEPT, POINTER and TALLYING, inline PERFORM VARYING, REDEFINES, reference modification, a second control item of the same report

probes.printed: EXIT 65; COBOL2378 at each of the 19 storing statements (ADD, COMPUTE, MULTIPLY GIVING, DIVIDE REMAINDER, MOVE to REDEFINES, MOVE to containing group, MOVE to CTL2 (2:1), STRING INTO, UNSTRING INTO, UNSTRING POINTER, UNSTRING TALLYING, INSPECT REPLACING, INSPECT TALLYING, ACCEPT FROM DATE, ACCEPT, inline PERFORM VARYING, INITIALIZE group, SUBTRACT, MOVE inside IF), each citing ISO §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR4
probes.expected: each statement refused: "A USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not alter the value of any control data item"

probes.printed: USE 01 QXYZ 1 / USE 02 QXYZ 2 / END 02 QXYZ 2 (EXIT 0)
probes.expected: MOVE to RDF (3:4) and OTH (1:1) touch no byte of CTL and are legal; the procedure runs once per GENERATE

probes.printed: MOVE SPACES TO GRP (group holding CTL) and INITIALIZE GRP refused; MOVE to RDF REDEFINES GRP refused
probes.expected: refused: a store into a group or redefinition holding the control data item alters it

probes.printed: accepted at --std 85; END 09 (PERFORM from the USE BEFORE REPORTING section of a paragraph in a USE AFTER ERROR section that MOVEs 9 to CTL)
probes.expected: SR4 governs the statements of the procedure; unlike SR3, SR4 does not extend to a PERFORM range, so no compile-time refusal is required

OK  §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR3  (4.9.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3
OK  §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR1  (4.9.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: Every storing statement form available at 1985 that reaches a control data item, directly, through a containing group, a REDEFINES, reference modification or an implicit operand, is refused with COBOL2378 at --std 85, and a store into bytes of a group or redefinition outside the control item is admitted and runs correctly. A store in a procedure PERFORMed from another declarative section is not refused; SR4, unlike SR3's PERFORM-range sentence, speaks of the procedure's own statements, so this is read as conforming. A CALL BY REFERENCE of a control item is not refused (the called program is not visible).

refuter.evidence: Read ReportWriterBinder.CheckControlDataStores/SameStorageLine, StatementBinder.BindStatement (lines 489-498), BoundStores.StoresInto and its StoreKindVisitor arms, PlaceBuilder.ConnectorStores. Probes at --std 85 (run_probe.py, refute-1985-247/runs): ubr_more.cob EXIT 65 with COBOL2378 at every new storing form the reader did not try: SET index-data-item TO index-name (a control data item may be an index data item, §1985:XIII.3.7.4 GR3), SEARCH VARYING the index data item, STRING WITH POINTER, INSPECT CONVERTING, DIVIDE INTO, MULTIPLY BY, MOVE CORRESPONDING and ADD CORRESPONDING into a corresponding control item, ACCEPT FROM TIME, UNSTRING DELIMITER IN / COUNT IN, READ of a file whose SAME RECORD AREA partner holds the control item, a store nested in AT END, out-of-line PERFORM VARYING ... AFTER the control item, ADD GIVING, and a store into the control item of ANOTHER report (R2) from R1's USE procedure. ubr_cd.cob and ubr_cdout.cob: control items in input and output CDs, refused for ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT, RECEIVE, SEND, ENABLE and DISABLE (status key). ubr_samearea.cob: SAME AREA (not RECORD) partner READ admitted, EXIT 0, 'END 01'. No under- or over-rejection found among the statement forms. What the verdict rests on: the reader's ubr_perform.cob (USE procedure PERFORMs a paragraph of another declarative section that MOVEs into the control item) compiles and prints END 09. SR4 is silent on PERFORM ranges; the reader reads it lexically by contrast with SR3's explicit PERFORM-range sentence. The other reading: SR3's first sentence is lexical ('must not appear in a paragraph') and so needed the PERFORM extension, while SR4 states an effect of the procedure ('must not alter the value'), which the procedure has when a statement of it PERFORMs a store; and since §1985:XIII.4.9.4 GR2 bars any reference to nondeclarative procedures, every range a USE procedure can PERFORM lies in the declaratives and is visible in the source element, so the effect is statically checkable (unlike a CALL BY REFERENCE, also not refused). cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR4 'A USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure must not alter the value of any control data item'; OK §1985:XIII.4.9.3 SR3; OK §1985:XIII.3.7.4 GR3; OK §1985:XIII.4.9.4 GR2 'there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures'.

adjudication.reason: Read again in slice 1985-247 after kb/Work PB5890 landed: every storing form refused, legal stores run. The doubt (a store through a PERFORM into another declarative section) is rejected: SR3 reaches a PERFORM's range and SR4 does not, so SR4 constrains the procedure's own statements.
